requested_parts: Whether damaged Invaders/Dahan deal less Damage
Combined Defend 1 and 2 applied to land/Dahan
answers.answer: Marked Damage does not reduce outgoing Damage from a piece. Defend effects add, so Defend 1 + Defend 2 reduces the 4 Damage separately for land and Dahan to 1 Damage each.

evidence.text: Matching lands with Invaders Ravage. Total the Damage: **1 per Explorer +2 per Town +3 per City**, then apply Defend and other explicit modifiers. Damage already marked on a piece does not reduce its outgoing Damage. Invaders deal the resulting Damage **equally, separately and simultaneously** to the land and its Dahan:

**Defend N** reduces each occurrence of Invader Damage to both land and Dahan by N for this turn, to a minimum of zero. Multiple Defend effects add. It does not reduce Spirit Damage or make Dahan do less counterattack Damage. Land and Dahan receive the reduction separately, not by splitting a shared allowance. A protection explicitly limited to Dahan is different: **Concealing Shadows** makes Dahan take no Damage from Ravaging Invaders this turn, while land still takes its normal Damage and can Blight. Protected surviving Dahan then counterattack normally. It does not protect them from direct Destroy instructions or Damage from other sources. [FAQ .7w4g8nu; original card text]

requested_parts: Fear and survival after Town-to-Explorer replacement retaining 1 Damage
Reduced Health without new Damage
answers.answer: The replacement itself produces no Fear. The Explorer has Health 1, so retained 1 Damage destroys it and normal Explorer destruction adds no Fear. Reduced Health can also destroy a piece already bearing enough Damage, without new Damage.

evidence.text: **Destroy** returns pieces to supply regardless of Health when directly instructed. Every destroyed Town generates **1 Fear** and every destroyed City **2 Fear**, in addition to explicit Fear from the effect. Explorers generate none automatically. **Remove** returns the specified pieces without requiring Damage to reach their Health and without destruction Fear. Within the effect's count and piece-type restrictions, its decision-maker may choose any eligible pieces; there is no Explorer-first priority unless stated. **Replace** removes a piece and adds another, retaining its marked Damage: the replacement itself produces no Fear, but if the retained Damage destroys the new piece, destruction Fear applies normally. For simultaneous replacements, select all pieces before replacing any: the same original City cannot become a Town and then an Explorer within that one simultaneous instruction. Separate completed instructions or actions may replace the resulting piece again (e.g., successive players resolving **Trade Suffers** at Terror III).

“Damage” means **Damage to Invaders** unless explicitly stated otherwise. Normal Spirit Damage does not harm Dahan or the land. Distribute Damage among Invaders in the target land however you wish; Explorers need not be hit first. Damage from separate normal Powers and counterattacks can accumulate within a turn. A piece is destroyed immediately when its marked Damage reaches/exceeds its Health. Reduced Health can also destroy a previously damaged piece; Damage does not itself reduce Health. If a damaged piece moves out of a Health bonus or into a Health penalty and is thereby destroyed, destruction occurs in its destination land, never in an in-between location. [FAQ if-an-invader-with-health-bonus-and-damage-is-moved-where-is-it-destroyed]

clause_coverage_check.clause: Fear and survival after Town-to-Explorer replacement retaining 1 Damage
clause_coverage_check.ruling: No replacement Fear; Explorer is destroyed by retained Damage, with no automatic Fear for Explorer.

clause_coverage_check.ruling: Yes.

requested_parts: Mandatory Gather/Push 3 when three legal pieces exist
When only two are available
Whether unrestricted Move may stay in same land
answers.answer: Without “up to,” Gather/Push 3 is mandatory to the extent possible: move all three if available, but only two when only two can be moved. An unrestricted Move can send a piece to its current land and still counts as movement.

evidence.text: **Gather N:** Move N of the specified pieces from adjacent land(s) into the target land. **Push N:** Move N from the target to adjacent land(s). Multiple pieces may come from or go to different adjacent lands. A numeric instruction without “up to” is mandatory to the extent possible; “up to” may be zero. Increased Power Range does **not** increase Gather/Push distance. Ordinary movement cannot send pieces off the island or into the Ocean; explicit Spirit rules can change Ocean legality.

A land is not adjacent to itself, so cannot Gather/Push to itself. It is at Range 0 of itself and hence within any greater Range. An unrestricted “Move” can move a piece to its current land and counts as movement, unlike Gather/Push, which require adjacency.

requested_parts: Difference between Move Presence and Add Presence repositioning
Whether an Add Presence disk can be picked up from outside destination Range
answers.answer: Move Presence moves a specified disk from its current location up to the shown distance. Add Presence/reposition first measures Range to the destination using existing Presence, including the disk being repositioned, then takes a disk from anywhere on the island. Thus the disk’s starting location need not be within the shown Range of the destination.

evidence.text: - **Move Presence:** A curved movement arrow moves the specified Presence from its present location up to the shown distance; this differs from Add/reposition. Push/Gather Presence uses normal adjacency rules. Instructions are mandatory where possible; a move up to a Range can be zero.

- **Add Presence:** Choose a legal land within the shown maximum Range of your existing Presence. Take the leftmost remaining disk from either Presence track and add it there. With multiple placements, resolve them sequentially: a newly placed disk may be the origin for the next. You may instead **reposition any of your island Presence**, even with track disks remaining: first measure range and select the destination using existing Presence, including the disk about to be repositioned, then take a disk from anywhere on the island. This is still an Add Presence instruction, not a Move instruction. Destroyed Presence cannot be used unless explicitly permitted.

Separate Forget for two Major gains
Ordinary Forgotten Unique reclaim
answers.answer: A gifted/transferred Major does not require Forgetting. Each Major gained requires its own Forget, so one Forget cannot cover two gains. A forgotten Unique is placed under the Spirit panel and cannot be ordinarily reclaimed or gained.

evidence.text: An effect that **gifts/transfers** a Major, or explicitly says to **take** one without Forgetting, differs from gaining it. A gain still requires Forgetting unless explicitly exempted. Follow the effect's wording. Cards gained enter hand unless explicitly placed elsewhere. Gaining during Growth allows playing that card in the later play/pay step; gaining it mid-turn does not by itself let you play it.

After **gaining a Major**, Forget one of your cards permanently. You may Forget from hand, personal discard, or play, including the Major just gained. A forgotten Minor/Major goes to its shared deck discard; a forgotten Unique goes under its Spirit panel, unavailable to ordinary Reclaim or gain. If you Forget from play, immediately lose its Elements and any unused activation; an already resolved effect persists normally. Each Major gained requires its own Forget; a single card cannot satisfy separate Forget requirements.

requested_parts: When choose card for Gift of Strength/Powerstorm Repeat
Whether chosen card may be Slow
Whether Innates may be repeated
Whether Repeat grants printed card Elements again
answers.answer: The card may be chosen when the Repeat is actually exercised, not when permission is granted; a later card in play that turn may qualify. Repeats use the Power’s currently assigned speed, so a Slow card can repeat in Slow. Gift of Strength and Powerstorm repeat Power Cards, not Innates. A Repeat does not grant printed card Elements again.

evidence.text: Retain changes to the Power, including extra Range or changed speed. An ordinary Repeat uses the Power's **most recently assigned speed**: a Slow Power repeats in Slow even if its permission came from a Fast Power; a formerly Fast Power explicitly made Slow before repeating now repeats in Slow. An instruction to Repeat immediately instead follows that explicit timing, directly after the originating use. [FAQ repeating-powers-with-changed-speeds] You may postpone choosing which eligible card to repeat until you actually repeat it, and make different choices/targets then. For **Powerstorm** and **Gift of Strength**, the Spirit receives a once-this-turn option rather than a grant-time selection of cards: a card played later that turn may be selected while it remains in play, subject to the permission’s restrictions and cost. [FAQ timing-of-choosing-powers-for-once-this-turn-repeats] Gift of Strength imposes its printed card-cost eligibility ceiling but requires no additional Energy payment for the Repeat, so an eligible card may be repeated with no Energy left. If the permission requires paying a cost, pay it as instructed. **Powerstorm** requires paying the repeated Power Card's Energy cost again when exercising each Repeat, including its threshold's further permissions; the original play payment does not cover it.

- **Repeat limits:** **Powerstorm** and **Gift of Strength** repeat Power **Cards**, not Innates. Powerstorm's threshold repeats up to three **different** cards. A Range/Speed change granted by a threshold carries to a Repeat even if that threshold is no longer met; it does not stack the same Range bonus again. [Core: .3y28aex, .7w4g8q9, Repeating-internal-range-boosts]

A Repeat activates a Power's effects again; it is not a second card play and grants no additional printed card Elements. It **does** count as another Power use. For effects counting cards played (such as Boon of Vigor), a Repeat adds no card play; count the card's original play only. A repeated effect explicitly granting Elements grants those again. Recheck thresholds using your current Elements; they were not spent on the original, but may since have been lost.

clause_coverage_check.ruling: No; selection can be postponed until exercise.
